messages.subject: problem with raster plot refreshing
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

i'm working a shiny app that plot a raster layer and when you click on the plot thath makes a time series, a kernel density and other stuff. I'm trying to make that when you click the plot it also plot the coordinates points, but when this happens the plot refresh.

I'm using a function to plot an this is the server part of the script:

Extract coordinates
  #defining raster click options
  Coords<- reactive({
    req(input$rasPlot_click$x)
    c(input$rasPlot_click$x,input$rasPlot_click$y)
  })

#EVI, anomalies & probabilitie selectable plot
  output$rasPlot <- renderPlot({
      dinput <- input$fechas

      data <- switch(input$dataset,
                     "EVI" = "EVI",
                     "Anomalia" = "Anomalia",
                     "Probabilidad" = "Probabilidad")
      color <- switch(input$dataset,
                      "EVI" = "EVI",
                      "Anomalia" = "Anomalia",
                      "Probabilidad" = "Probabilidad")
      rango <- switch(input$dataset,
                      "EVI" = "EVI",
                      "Anomalia" = "Anomalia",
                      "Probabilidad" = "Probabilidad")

      x <- reactive({input$rasPlot_click$x})
      y <- reactive({input$rasPlot_click$y})

      plot_index(data = data,color = color,range = rango,dinput = dinput,x=x(),y=y()) ###function thath make the raster plot

  },height = 650,width = 650,res = 120)

plot_index function

plot_index<-function(data, color, range, dinput,x,y){

  if(data == "EVI")
    rast<- stack("./data/EVI.tif")
  if(data == "Anomalia")
    rast <- stack("./data/Anom.tif")
  if(data == "Probabilidad")
    rast <- stack("./data/Prob.tif")

  if(data == "EVI")
    paleta<- c('#f7fcfd','#e5f5f9','#ccece6','#99d8c9','#66c2a4','#41ae76','#238b45','#006d2c','#00441b')
  if(data == "Anomalia")
    paleta<- c('#b2182b','#d6604d','#f4a582','#fddbc7','#f7f7f7','#d1e5f0','#92c5de','#4393c3','#2166ac')
  if(data == "Probabilidad")
    paleta<-c ("#fff7ec","#fee8c8","#fdd49e","#fdbb84","#fc8d59","#ef6548","#d7301f","#b30000",
               "#7f0000")

  if(data == "EVI")
    z<-c(0,1)
  if(data == "Anomalia")
    z<-c(-0.3,0.3)
  if(data == "Probabilidad")
    z<-c(0,100)

  #Read dates
  dates.table<-read.csv("./data/all_791_dates.csv", sep = ",", header=T)
  dates <-as.Date(dates.table$date, format='%d/%m/%Y')
  PNLC <- readOGR(dsn = "./data", layer = "pn_la_campana")
  PNLC<-spTransform(x = PNLC,CRSobj = "+proj=utm +zone=19 +south +datum=WGS84 +units=m +no_defs")
  dateSelect<-which(dates==dinput)
  lat<-y
  lon<-x
  plot((rast[[dateSelect]]/10000), col=paleta, zlim=z)
  plot(PNLC,add=T)#"+proj=utm +zone=19 +south +datum=WGS84 +units=m +no_defs"
  points(lon,lat,pch=13)

  #plot(OC, add=T,color=rgb(0,0,0,alpha=1), border="transparent")

}

messages.subject: Is it possible to show a widget as often as entered in the Input? so a dynamic input / UI?
messages.subject_clean: Is it possible to show a widget as often as entered in the Input? so a dynamic input / UI?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I’m building a Shiny App. However, there is something which doesn’t work and I hope someone can help me out.

At the first button, it must be possible for the user to enter a number. This I have done through the following code:

#First button
numericInput("numberofx",
        label = ("Number of x")

When someone enters 1, the next button (the selectInput button) must appear once. But if someone 2 enters at the first button, this (second) button must appear twice and so on. This second button must therefore be displayed just as often as entered in the first button. This is the second button:

selectInput("kind",
      label = ("kind"),
      choices = list(
              "Choice 1" = "1",
              "Choice 2" = "2",
              "Choice 3" = "3",
            selected = 1)

I was thinking about something like:
for ( i in 1:input$numberofx) {selectInput("kind",

                         label = ("kind"),
                         choices = list(
                           "Choice 1" = "1",
                           "Choice 2" = "2",
                           "Choice 3" = "3",
                         selected = 1)}

But that's not working unluckily. Could someone help me with this?

This is the full code:
shinyApp(

  ui = navbarPage(
    tabPanel(title = "Invulformulier",

             numericInput("numberofx",
                          label = ("Number of x"),
                          value = NA),

             #This widget should appear in the app as often as it is entered in the previous widget
             selectInput("kind",
                         label = ("kind"),
                         choices = list(
                           "Choice 1" = "1",
                           "Choice 2" = "2",
                           "Choice 3" = "3",
                         selected = 1)
             )))

Many thanks in advance!!

messages.subject: Marginal Frequency Table format
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
     I was hoping on rendering a marginal frequency table to look nice. When I convert the table from crosstab() to Table() it messes up the format. Is there a way to keep the frequency table formatted correctly?

###########################################################################
################################# UI ######################################
###########################################################################

# First we load the required packages
library(shiny) # for the website functions
library(DT)    # For the tabling functions

### Create some data to play with ###
Individual <- 1:1000
Population <- rep.int <http://rep.int/>(c("Adult", "Children"), 500)
Bloodcount <- rnorm(1000, mean = 500, sd = 56 )  # Random Blood counts
Exp <- rbinom(n=1000, size=1, prob=0.5)  # Random 1/0's
Disease <- rbinom(n=1000, size=1, prob=0.22) # Random 1/0s
Data <- data.frame(Individual, Population, Bloodcount, Exp, Disease) # put all of this into a dataset called Data

# Define User Interface
ui <- fluidPage(

  # Application title
  titlePanel("Marginal Crosstable example"),

  # Sidebar with a slider input for number of bins
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(  )                                                    # Start to create the sidepanel

    mainPanel(

      tableOutput('Table')       # output the Table

    )      # Close mainpanel
  )      # Close sidebar
)       ## Close UI

###########################################################################
#############################  Server  ####################################
###########################################################################

server <- function(input, output) {
  source("http://pcwww.liv.ac.uk/~william/R/crosstab.r")                                                    # Import the crossTable function

  # Create the Table
  output$Table <- renderTable({

                                             Table.Data   <- crosstab(Data, row.vars = "Exp", col.vars = "Disease", type = "f")                     # Create the crosstab table

                                            Table.Data$"table"                                                                                                                            # Produce the table

  })

  } # Close Server end

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

This all works when I am running my App on my local R program. However, I'm building this App for a company and they will run this App on a server. Now my question is: Is it possible to upload the information from my Shiny App directly to Google drive? Since it is not possible to save the data to as a local file first when I am running the app on the server.
